messages:
sam: Heads up — after the CNI upgrade to cilium-1.24.2 in us-west2-gpu we see intermittent pod-to-pod UDP drops and ~10-30ms extra tail latency for east-west traffic. Started ~03:10 UTC during the batch rollout.
lara: ack. Which node pools are hit? only GPU nodes?
sam: Mostly gpu-pool-3 and -4 (A100s). Non-gpu clusters look fine. Failing jobs are our nightly evals and some in-flight training checkpoints that hit RPC timeouts.
maria: any packet capture or iperf outputs? can we reproduce on-node?
sam: ran a quick iperf3 between two affected pods, short run:
```
iperf3 -c 10.2.8.41 -u -b 5G -t 10
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  5.00 GBytes  4.29 Gbits/sec  (loss=12%)
```
loss spikes inconsistent. tcp looks mostly ok but UDP is flaky.
dilip: UDP loss + GPUs + cilium upgrade screams offload/tunnel MTU mismatch to me. Did the upgrade flip tunnel mode or encap settings?
sam: rollout notes show "enable-bpf-gso: true" and a geneve MTU auto-detect tweak. We also flipped featureFlag:enableHybridEncap in the helm values.
irene: @sam can you paste `ip link` + `ethtool -k` for the host NIC (one affected node) and the pod veth?
sam: pasted below from node gpu-34:
```
# ip link show ens18
3: ens18: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# ethtool -k ens18
Generic Segmentation Offload: on
Generic Receive Offload: on
TCP segmentation offload: on
UDP fragmentation offload: off
```
pod veth shows mtu 1450.
lara: mtu mismatch ens18(9000) vs pod veth(1450) could cause fragmentation at encap layer. geneve/gso interplay can drop packets if UDP fragmentation is happening and offloads are enabled/disabled asymmetrically.
maria: Also saw a kernel bug on 5.10 w/ GSO + geneve that triggers on heavy UDP streams. What kernel are the nodes on?
sam: 5.10.92-gke (managed image).
dilip: that matches. Quick mitigation options: 1) roll back cilium to pre-upgrade (1.24.0), 2) disable bpf-gso feature, or 3) force MTU alignment (set pod MTU to 8900) while we investigate.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1843 — "us-west2-gpu inter-pod UDP loss after CNI upgrade". Pager notified.
irene: We should also check rdma/ib devices — are we accidentally routing RDMA traffic through the geneve tunnel? That would kill perf for some training.
sam: RDMA interfaces are present on these nodes. ib0 exists but our pod affinity pins RDMA pods to node-local SR-IOV. Still worth validating.
lara: Immediate plan: can we patch the daemonset to set enable-bpf-gso=false as a canary on one AZ? If that stabilizes, escalate to full rollback.
maria: Agree. Also capture tcpdump on both host and inside pod with `-s 0 -w /tmp/udp-drop.pcap` for a few minutes while we trigger iperf. This will let us see if fragmentation is lost pre/post encap.
dilip: I'll prepare a helm rollback PR (pin cilium to 1.24.0) and a small patch to flip bpf-gso off. Which one do we try first?
sam: let's try bpf-gso=false on a single node pool first (gpu-pool-3 canary). If that doesn't help, rollback.
lara: scheduling canary now — patch applied to gpu-pool-3 via k8s-deploy-bot.
k8s-deploy-bot: Deployment 'cilium-ds' updated in namespace kube-system (canary: gpu-pool-3). Image: quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.24.2; args: --disable-bpf-gso
sam: early signal — iperf loss dropped to ~1% on canary node. RPC timeouts reduced for one job.
imene: typo — (meant to be irene) — good sign. Can we run longer tests (8-12h) before a full rollback?
dilip: note: rollback will affect non-gpu clusters if we do cluster-level helm rolls. We should scope to node pools.
maria: also open ticket with GKE to check kernel+GSO interactions; may be a managed image kernel backport issue.
lara: oncall will keep watch and throttle GPU provisioning for non-essential batch jobs to preserve capacity for prod. We may move some long-running training off us-west2 until stable. Cost impact: reduced throughput may increase runtime by ~12% for queued jobs — heads up to finance.
oncall-bot: Pager cleared for now — monitoring.
sam: will keep thread updated. If canary stays healthy for 6h, we'll roll the rest of gpu-pool-4 and -5 with the bpf-gso toggle.
maria: and collect pcaps and ethtool dumps for postmortem.
lara: thanks everyone, good catch.
